task: Assistant-reviewed large/touching colony and real empty-plate data for retention training
annotationIdentity: Codex visual annotations and corrections, not certified microbiologist ground truth
target: Visually distinguishable macroscopic colony instances on agar photographs; not individual microscopic cells
positiveRules: Inspect each accepted photograph at sufficient resolution and record the review and any corrected geometry.
Author boxes or masks may initialize proposals, but provenance must distinguish reused, accepted-after-review, corrected and newly drawn annotations.
Label all countable visible colonies in an accepted full image; do not silently omit difficult regions.
Touching colonies may have separate instances only when separate centers/boundaries are visually resolvable.
Quarantine unresolved confluent lawns or uncertain counts; do not invent instance counts or label these as background.
Explicit crops may exclude an uncertain region, but retain original-image/physical-plate grouping and crop transforms.
negativeRules: A zero label means no visible colony in the photograph, not a microbiological sterility claim.
Inspect real plate surface, rims, glare and suspicious specks; quarantine uncertain growth.
Uncountable or clinical-negative class names alone never imply zero visible colonies.
Pure color controls supplement real empty plates and are never counted as newly collected real data.
separationRules: Freeze image/annotation hashes and physical-plate or conservative acquisition groups before model evaluation.
Variants, crops, lighting views and near duplicates of a plate remain in the same partition.
Keep all previous frozen labels, failed experiments and model artifacts unchanged.
No prior validation/test image may enter the new training loss.
The previously reserved 36 clinical test images remain excluded from development.
acceptance: A new candidate must improve hard-case validation and pass strict zero-regression comparisons against the actual frozen old-v2 automatic4tile/confidence0.3 baseline. Prior failed stronger-reference protocols remain preserved as separate experiments.
